page_title: Face recognition MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor — SightRadar

sources.entry: SightRadar Face Recognition API MCP - Official MCP server for the SightRadar face recognition API: index photos, find every photo of a person from one selfie, and compare or detect faces from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or VS Code. Add https://mcp.sightradar.com/mcp as an MCP server, or run it locally with npx. #paid #mcp #opensource

summary.name: SightRadar Face Recognition MCP Server
summary.one_liner: A hosted and npm-installable MCP server that lets Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or VS Code index photos, find a person from a selfie, and compare or detect faces via the SightRadar face recognition API.
use_cases: Find every photo of a person from one selfie
Index a photo library for face search
Compare two images to check whether faces match
Detect faces in images from an AI assistant
Connect face recognition to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or VS Code
summary.what_it_does: The page describes an MCP server that exposes 39 SightRadar face recognition tools to AI assistants. Tools are grouped into read, search, write, delete and account permissions, and the user chooses which groups to grant during OAuth approval. Search tools cover searching, detecting and comparing faces, and the write tools create collections, index photos, register selfies and submit batches. A hosted endpoint at mcp.sightradar.com/mcp requires no install; a local npm package (sightradar-mcp, run with npx and an API key) offers the same tools and can read image files from allowed folders. Each tool call is billed as a normal API call from prepaid credits, priced per photo rather than per face.
notable: 39 tools across read, search, write, delete and account permission groups, with the user choosing which groups to grant
API key is created per connection and kept away from the AI app; OAuth tokens are used instead
Open-source local option via npx sightradar-mcp that can read image files from allowed folders
No MCP fee; tool calls billed at the normal per-photo API price
caveats: Every call spends prepaid credits (for example 93 credits per photo for search or detect, 62 per photo for batches); reading and deleting are free
Account-level tools can change auto-recharge and may charge a card; they are off by default
Selfies are biometric data and should be registered only with the person's consent, per the Acceptable Use Policy
Local server needs Node.js 20 or newer; the hosted server accepts image URLs or base64 data rather than local files
